 Ross Coulthart wants closer look at Alaska ‘jellyfish’ UFO before final verdict 
 Tatiana Carter 
 Updated: Nov 16, 2026 / 07:33 AM CST 
 Comments: 
 ( NewsNation ) — Was the jellyfish-shaped UFO filmed over Alaska just a kite all along, or is there more to it? NewsNation’s Ross Coulthart says he can’t offer a view one way or another, and he wants to see a more careful look before anyone declares the mystery solved. 
 Coulthart discussed the video on “Reality Check with Ross Coulthart,” in a Q&A that premiered Sunday, in conversation with NewsNation’s Meagan Medick , host of “Unreported.”
 What does Stephen Miller as chief of staff mean for UFO disclosure? 
 The video, shot by Sara Osborn in June, captured a floating object that appeared to have tentacles near Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson before it disappeared a few minutes later.
 Screen grab detail of a jellyfish-looking object in Alaska (Sara Osborn) 
 The kite explanation has plenty of support, including from skeptic Mick West and from two UAP experts who told NewsNation’s Jesse Weber they lean toward a kite or a high-altitude balloon. Coulthart said West raised useful points, among them that kites were being flown in the area, that the wind that day fits how the object moved, and that jellyfish-style kites are actually called “UFO kites.”
 UFO legacy program? Trump would have sniffed it out, scientist says 
 Even so, Coulthart said he wants to hear from the person who created the video. 
 “I’d like to hear from the woman who shot the video to see if that’s what she thinks,” he said, adding that he read she and her partner drove around looking for kite flyers and found none, though he doesn’t know whether that came from her directly.
 Fake footage makes investigating these kinds of phenomena harder, too. Coulthart said he sees “probably a hundred AI-generated videos that get sent to me every week,” which he said undermine the assessment of objects that could be genuinely anomalous.
